question: For each rating category of the first movie rented by customers—where the first movie is identified based on the earliest payment date per customer—please provide the average total amount spent per customer and the average number of subsequent rentals (calculated as the total number of rentals minus one) for customers whose first rented movie falls into that rating category.
sql:
WITH first_payment AS (
    SELECT customer_id, payment_id, rental_id
    FROM (
        SELECT customer_id, payment_id, rental_id,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date) as rn
        FROM payment
    )
    WHERE rn = 1
),
first_rental AS (
    SELECT fp.customer_id, fp.rental_id
    FROM first_payment fp
),
first_film AS (
    SELECT fr.customer_id, fr.rental_id, r.inventory_id, i.film_id
    FROM first_rental fr
    JOIN rental r ON fr.rental_id = r.rental_id
    JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
),
first_rating AS (
    SELECT ff.customer_id, ff.film_id, f.rating
    FROM first_film ff
    JOIN film f ON ff.film_id = f.film_id
),
customer_amount AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, SUM(p.amount) as total_amount
    FROM customer c
    JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
customer_rentals AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.rental_id) as total_rentals
    FROM customer c
    LEFT JOIN rental r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
)
SELECT 
    fr.rating,
    AVG(ca.total_amount) as avg_total_amount,
    AVG(cr.total_rentals - 1) as avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM first_rating fr
JOIN customer_amount ca ON fr.customer_id = ca.customer_id
JOIN customer_rentals cr ON fr.customer_id = cr.customer_id
GROUP BY fr.rating
ORDER BY fr.rating
